messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: High error rate and connection stalls observed from several ap-svc clusters in us-east-1. Severity: P1. Paging #oncall rota -> @kevin (pagerduty). 2955012345

pagerduty: Pager duty alert: page to kevin (oncall) — oncall acknowledgment required.

kevin (oncall): Acked — taking it. seeing 502/504 spike on /api/generate from ELB metrics. Load balancer latency up ~3x since 09:02 UTC. Investigating.

lucy (eng-runtime): I'm seeing persistent keepalive resets fronting the NLB to our pods. Logs show a lot of `connection reset by peer` from the ELB IPs. P95 CPU on runtime unchanged. No recent deploys.

raj (netops): Traceroutes from us-east-edge to backend AZs show asymmetric paths and elevated rtt on azb: `traceroute -n 10.0.3.5` -> some hops timing out between 54.239.x.x and 15.230.x.x. Might be regional routing steering in AWS.

kevin (oncall): Can we confirm Route53 healthchecks? lucy, any recent DNS TTL or weighted routing changes?

lucy (eng-runtime): No config changes from our side. Route53 healthchecks for ap-svc are green from most locations but eu-west probe shows timeout. Healthcheck logs: `HTTP 200` from 10/12 collectors, but 2 collectors report `timeout`.

maria (support): We have 3 related customer tickets claiming slow responses and errors during 09:00-09:10 UTC. CS triage says impact: heavy for customers in eastern US, intermittent for EU.

erin (product): Customer impact note: primary traffic (api key scopes) to hosted API likely affected. Need a public post if we can't mitigate in 30m.

kevin (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) shift Route53 weight away from us-east-azb 2) move ELB listener healthcheck to N target pool draining to reduce sticky connections 3) open AWS support case. Luc y/raj can you run the shift?

lucy (eng-runtime): Starting weighted shift now: updated Route53 record to drop weight on us-east-azb from 0.35 -> 0.0, redistributed to usw2 and us-east-aza. CLI command used: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://shift-2955012345.json` (applied).

raj (netops): Confirmed change propagated to nameservers. Also adding secondary edge-route steering: modifying ELB cross-zone load balancing target group priorities. Doing `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10` to speed drain.

incidents-bot: NOTE: Change recorded in incident timeline by kevin.

kevin (oncall): After shift, errors dropped from 18% -> 3% within 2 min for affected customers. Latency returned near baseline. Keeping monitoring an extra 30m.

lucy (eng-runtime): Observed a residual spike of TCP RSTs from an AWS edge IP block: `tcpdump` snippet: `IP 15.230.12.5 > 10.0.3.12: RST`. Looks like an ELB front-end issue causing mid-stream resets. Opening case with AWS with these captures.

aws-case-bot: Case opened with AWS Support: case# 1122334455. Severity: urgent. Uploading tcpdump and ELB access logs.

raj (netops): AWS status page shows a partial networking issue in us-east-1 affecting select AZ fabric (notice: some customers observing increased TCP resets). This matches our symptom set.

maria (support): Updating customer tickets: noting we rerouted traffic and are monitoring. ETA for full resolution unknown, advise retry/backoff and short-term increase client timeouts.

erin (product): Sending internal comms: draft status update -> "Partial connectivity disruptions for east coast customers; we have shifted traffic and are monitoring; workaround applied." Will post if AWS doesn't confirm resolution in 45m.

kevin (oncall): Handoff: I'll remain on for now until AWS confirms edge fabric restoration. If any more degradation, escalate to SRE lead. @lucy keep me posted on error trends.

lucy (eng-runtime): Will do. Adding quick healthcheck to internal dashboard to track ELB 5xx + TCP resets.

incidents-bot: Update: route53 change at 09:05 applied, ELB attribute modify at 09:07.

kevin (oncall): Status check 09:18: error rate steady ~2-4%, p95 latency ~1.2x baseline. Customers reporting much improved. Rolling out rollback of weight after AWS confirms.

aws-case-bot: AWS responded: "Investigating partial networking degradation in us-east-1 AZB; engineers deployed mitigation for affected load balancers. Monitoring for stability." Case updated.

raj (netops): Recommend leaving weight reduced for 45 more minutes to ensure no oscillation during AWS mitigation windows.

maria (support): Customer update posted to affected tickets and status page draft queued.

erin (product): I'll prepare a short postmortem template for the follow-up: timeline, root cause (AWS AZ fabric), mitigation (traffic shift), customer impact, next steps (failover automation, healthcheck diversity).

kevin (oncall): Closing notes: Incident categorized as third-party networking (AWS us-east AZB). No internal config change caused this. Postmortem owners: lucy + raj + erin. I'll hand off to them when I'm offcall. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring. Change state to MONITORING at 09:35 UTC.

maria (support): Marking tickets as monitoring, will update if customers reopen.

lucy (eng-runtime): Captures and logs uploaded to incident folder: `/incidents/2955012345/` (elb logs, tcpdump, route53 change log). Will assemble detailed timeline.

kevin (oncall): Handing off—oncall rotation ends in 20m. If regression, page the SRE lead. Good job everyone.

(End of thread)
